name: Slotwise — the picking floor that explains itself
one_liner: A browser-native 3D digital twin of one real month of Online Retail II orders where every number has a slider, every slot shows why it is there, the before/after is a ghost race on the same orders, and the slotting optimizer anneals your layout live in 3D while you can grab boxes and fight it.
why_it_wins: Four scouts converge on 4.2; my lens makes it decisive rather than default. An explorable explanation needs the FULL objective to re-evaluate at slider speed with no network: in 4.2 the objective is "replay ~3k real orders through an aisle graph" and that is 50–300 ms in a Web Worker, so walking speed, pick time, cross-aisle toggle, routing policy, order-size filter and the month scrubber all re-flow the KPIs within a frame. 4.3's solver needs seconds plus a Python backend (cold start, cargo-transfer trap); 2.3's model is frozen ONNX (only the threshold is manipulable); 3.3 is a rules table. Only 4.2 lets the judge touch the model itself. What a judge remembers: (1) the ghost race, two pickers walking the same real invoice on old and new layouts with counters diverging live; (2) "watch it think": simulated annealing physically swapping boxes in 3D with its energy curve drawing itself, the judge pausing it, dragging a hot SKU by hand, and the annealer continuing from the human's state (co-op optimisation); (3) every slot answers "why are you here?" with pick count, distance to dock, co-pick partners drawn as lines, and a one-move lookahead delta. The must-have IS the 3D, so every hour of polish is an hour on requirements. Zero backend, zero keys, zero rate limits, zero cold start: the safest live demo of the twelve, deterministic (seed on screen) so judges can click Replay twice. Low pick rate (three.js scares ML students) with the highest reward. Evaluation is baked into the design: chronological held-out split (1–15 Nov tune, 16–30 Nov held-out), a real optimizer baseline the player must beat, exact per-order routing (Held–Karp) so distances are a bound not a guess, and a one-command eval that reproduces every number on screen.
demo_script:
Pre-demo: app open at the deployed URL in a clean Chrome profile at 125% zoom, quality toggle "High" verified at >45 fps on the demo laptop (else "Low"), backup MP4 on two laptops, phone hotspot ready. One operator, one narrator.

0:00–0:25 HOOK. Isometric camera slowly orbits the floor (8 aisles, 112 slots, dock front-left). Narrator: "Pickers walk more than they pick. This is November 2011 of a real UK gift retailer, UCI Online Retail II: N orders, 100 SKUs, top-left counter shows lines covered / total (coverage X%). Nothing on this screen is pre-rendered; every number is computed from those orders right now." Order IDs stream past in the ticker.

0:25–1:05 M2 — ONE ORDER, VISIBLE REASONING. Operator clicks the hero invoice in the order list (script-chosen: 8–10 covered lines across ≥4 aisles). Camera flies to the dock (CameraControls.setLookAt tween); the cyan path draws itself ahead of the picker; the picker walks along aisles (never through racks); metres and seconds tick up. Operator flips Routing Policy from Optimal to S-shape: the path redraws, the order's distance rises on screen, the month total in the KPI bar rises too. WOW micro-moment 1: hover a slot: cause card appears ("85123A WHITE HANGING HEART T-LIGHT HOLDER, 412 picks, 14.2 m from dock, in 13% of orders; co-picked with 22423 (31%), 84879 (22%)") and affinity lines light up to those slots in 3D.

1:05–1:40 M3 — THE BASELINE. Press "ABC baseline". A two-column matching animation shows SKUs ranked by picks sliding into slots ranked by distance to dock, then the 100 boxes fly to their new slots in 3D (staggered tween). KPI table fills: Original vs ABC, tune set AND held-out set, distance km and avg pick time/order, with the % change counting up. Narrator: "That is the layout the player has to beat. It is measured, not claimed."

1:40–2:40 WOW 1 — WATCH IT THINK. Press "Optimize (watch)". The annealer runs in a worker at ~30 moves/s: boxes swap in 3D, green flash for improvements, amber for accepted uphill moves; the energy curve (total km vs iteration) draws itself with the temperature line decaying beneath it; the "affected orders" counter shows how many of the 3k orders were re-routed by each move. At ~30 s the operator hits PAUSE, drags a hot SKU from a far rack to the front: a toast explains the human move ("−0.9 km on 412 orders, +0.3 km on the 170 orders of the SKU it displaced, net −0.6 km"); hit RESUME: the annealer continues from the human's state, then "Finish fast" completes the remaining iterations in a few seconds. Narrator: "The optimizer sees order affinity that ABC cannot: products bought together end up neighbours. And you can argue with it."

2:40–3:30 WOW 2 — THE GHOST RACE. Press "Replay race". Two pickers start at the dock on the same held-out invoices: a translucent ghost on the ORIGINAL layout, a solid picker on the NEW one. Counters diverge live (Before / After / Δ%). Floor tiles under both paths accumulate heat (rack-visit heatmap). Camera "Follow" mode for 10 s, then back to isometric. Operator hits Replay twice: identical numbers (determinism, seed shown).

3:30–4:10 SLIDERS — THE MODEL IS TOUCHABLE. Pick time 8 s → 15 s: time KPIs re-flow, distance unchanged (shows what the objective is). Toggle "middle cross-aisle": the floor re-lays out in 3D, all totals re-score in <100 ms, the optimal routes shorten. Drag the month scrubber from 1 Nov to 30 Nov: the heatmap accumulates day by day, the KPI shows the prefix totals; stop at 15 Nov to point at the tune/held-out boundary.

4:10–4:40 EVIDENCE. Open the Evidence panel: the same table that `npm run eval` writes to eval/results.md (commit hash + timestamp shown): Original / ABC / SA(seed 42) / Player on tune and held-out; routing policy ablation (S-shape vs Return vs Optimal); coverage; "held-out gain smaller than in-sample gain" highlighted on purpose. Limitations card read aloud in one breath: one month, top-100 forward-pick area, declared original layout, one level, no congestion, constant pick time.

4:40–5:00 CLOSE. Save layout to the local leaderboard, export JSON, QR codes for live URL and repo. "Every member owns a module; ask us anything."
wow_visual: Scene (React Three Fiber 9.8.2 + drei 10.7.9 + three 0.186.1, Vite SPA, static): (1) Racks and floor as ONE InstancedMesh each (8 aisles × 2 sides × 7 bays = 112 slot cells, ~250 instances incl. uprights), `instanceColor` carries the rack-visit heat (viridis-like ramp from the per-order path results, prefix-summed for the month scrubber). (2) SKU boxes: 100 instanced boxes with drei `<Text>` (troika) labels showing StockCode, colour = pick-frequency rank; hover = emissive lift + cause card (`<Html>` anchored); selected = glow. (3) Picker: capsule body + two cylinder legs with sine bob, moving along the aisle-graph polyline at speed × replaySpeed; ghost picker = same mesh, `transparent opacity 0.35 wireframe`. (4) Self-drawing path: drei `<Line>` (Line2, 3 px, cyan, `dashed` for ghost) whose `points` slice grows per frame ahead of the picker; counters animated with `motion`'s `animate(from,to)`. (5) Camera choreography: drei `<CameraControls>` (camera-controls 3.1.2) presets Dock / Isometric / Top-down ortho (projection morph via `camera.zoom` + orthographic toggle) / Follow, all `setLookAt(...,true)` tweens. (6) Post-FX (`@react-three/postprocessing` 3.2.1, postprocessing 6.39.5): Bloom (luminanceThreshold 0.9, mipmapBlur) so only the path and selected box glow, SMAA, optional N8AO 2.0.1; quality toggle Low/High, auto-drop when FPS < 40 for 2 s; `dpr={[1,1.5]}`; `frameloop="demand"` while idle. (7) Box moves: ABC baseline and annealer swaps tween boxes along an arc (lerp in `useFrame`, 300 ms), staggered via a move queue; the ABC matching animation is a 2-column `motion` layout list (SKUs by picks ↔ slots by distance). (8) Optimizer panel: energy curve (km vs iteration) and temperature as SVG with d3-scale, drawn incrementally from worker ticks; move feed with green/amber chips. (9) Month scrubber: `@radix-ui/react-slider` over 1–30 Nov with a daily order-count sparkline; drives heat and KPI prefix sums (no recompute). (10) Dark high-contrast theme (Tailwind 4.3.3), fonts ≥16 px, projector-tested; top-left data badge (source, licence, coverage) always visible. Draw calls target < 150; verified in r3f-perf 7.2.3 during build, removed before freeze.
wow_technical:
Everything is one pure-TypeScript simulation module (`web/src/sim/`) shared by the Web Worker (scoring), the eval script (Node, `npm run eval`) and the animation (path arrays), so "score from the animation" is impossible by construction.
(1) Aisle graph: nodes = aisle cells (aisle k, bay j), front/back (optional middle) cross-aisle cells, dock; edges: bay pitch 1.5 m, cross-aisle hop 3.0 m, dock link 3.0 m. All-pairs Dijkstra (~130 nodes) rebuilt in ~10 ms when geometry sliders change; paths stored for animation. Slots on both sides of a bay share one aisle cell (stops dedupe).
(2) Exact per-order routing: Held–Karp bitmask DP (n ≤ 10 stops after dedupe, 10²·2¹⁰ ≈ 100k ops) returning the tour and its length; nearest-neighbour + 2-opt/Or-opt above 10; classical S-shape and Return policies implemented for ablation (Hall 1993 taxonomy). Vitest: DP equals brute force for n ≤ 7 on random matrices; S-shape never crosses a rack.
(3) Slotting optimizer = simulated annealing over the slot assignment with the TRUE replay objective (total exact-route distance over the tune set), made interactive by incremental delta evaluation: per-order route cost cache + inverted index SKU → orders; a swap of SKUs i,j re-routes only orders containing i or j (typically 1–15% of orders); route-cost memo keyed by the sorted aisle-cell set (many orders collapse to the same stop set). Moves: swap two occupied slots (80%), move to one of the 12 empty slots (20%), 50% biased to a top-30 SKU. T0 auto-calibrated so the median uphill move of 200 random swaps is accepted with p = 0.5; geometric cooling alpha = 0.995 per 100 iterations; 20k iterations default; mulberry32 PRNG with the seed displayed. Inner loop uses DP cap 8 (2-opt above) + memo for speed; final reported scores use the UI policy (DP cap 10). Expected ~10–20 s for a full run in "fast" mode, 30 moves/s in "watch" mode, with pause / step / inject (player's assignment replaces the current state and caches are invalidated for affected orders only). Why non-trivial: affinity-aware slotting is a quadratic-assignment-like problem; ABC/COI is the textbook greedy that ignores co-picks; SA on the replayed objective captures them, and the delta machinery is what makes it a live, interruptible search instead of a batch job.
(4) Explain-a-move: the same delta routine returns the breakdown (orders affected, km gained by the moved SKU, km lost by the displaced SKU) for the toast and the hover lookahead (debounced 50 ms while dragging).
(5) Evaluation: chronological split (1–15 Nov tune / 16–30 Nov held-out); SA sees only tune; metrics = total walking km and mean pick time per order (walk/speed + lines × pick s) for Original (StockCode-sorted, declared arbitrary), ABC baseline, SA(seed 42, also 5 seeds mean±sd), Player; routing-policy ablation on the same layouts; runtime per full score and per SA run. The proof metric: % distance reduction vs ABC on the HELD-OUT half (expected a few to ~10%, to be measured, with the in-sample number shown beside it so over-fitting is visible).
Worker protocol (so agents can build in parallel): INIT{data,layoutCfg} · SCORE{assignment,params,policy,set}→{km,s,perOrder:Float32Array} · DELTA{assignment,move}→{Δkm,breakdown} · ABC{}→assignment · PATH{orderIdx}→polyline · EXPLAIN_SLOT{slot}→card · ANNEAL_START{T0?,alpha,iters,seed,mode} / TICK events {iter,T,current,best,move,accepted,affected} / PAUSE / RESUME / INJECT{assignment} / FINISH.
mvp_mapping:
M1 (pre-processing → JSON): `prep/prep.py` (Python 3.12, pandas 3.0.6, pyarrow 26.0.0) reads the Online Retail II parquet, filters InvoiceDate in [2011-11-01, 2011-12-01), drops Invoice starting with "C", Quantity ≤ 0, Price ≤ 0, StockCodes not matching ^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$ (removes POST, D, M, S, DOT, BANK CHARGES, CRUK, ADJUST, AMAZONFEE, gift_*, C2, PADS, TEST*), exact duplicate rows; collapses to one pick line per (Invoice, StockCode); ranks SKUs by number of pick lines; keeps the top 100; emits `web/public/data/orders_2011-11.json`: meta (every cleaning count, coverage = covered lines / cleaned lines, licence, citation), skus [{code, desc, picks, qty, orders}], orders [{inv, ts, lines:[skuIdx]}] for every invoice with ≥1 covered line, split {tune: 1–15 Nov, test: 16–30 Nov}, top co-pick pairs. The in-app Data badge shows these counts; clicking any slot shows its StockCode, description and pick count from this JSON.
M2 (3D twin replaying orders): R3F scene with 8 aisles, racks on both sides, front/back cross-aisles, packing dock, one animated picker; selecting any order makes the picker walk the aisle graph (Dijkstra paths, never through racks) to each slot and back to the dock with the path drawn on the floor and live distance (m) and time (s) counters; auto-replay mode streams orders in timestamp order with the invoice ID on screen and month totals accumulating.
M3 (game mode): click-to-select then click-to-swap (primary) and drei DragControls drag-and-drop with snap (secondary) move SKUs between slots, including the 12 empty slots; "Replay" re-scores exactly the same order list headlessly in the worker and shows Before / After distance km, avg pick time per order and Δ%, on tune and held-out sets; "ABC baseline" button generates the fast-movers-nearest-dock layout (SKUs by picks ↔ slots by distance-to-dock) and its score sits in the KPI table as the target to beat; layouts are saved/loaded as JSON.
stretch_goals: Heatmap of rack visits (instanceColor from per-order paths, month scrubber prefix sums) — nearly free once M2 exists
Leaderboard of player layouts (localStorage + JSON export/import; stated as per-browser, no backend)
Co-op optimizer: pause/inject/resume the annealer with the player's manual swaps; explain-a-move toasts; hover lookahead delta
Routing-policy ablation in-app and in eval (S-shape vs Return vs NN+2-opt vs Optimal) on the same layouts
Batch picking: cart of capacity C orders, seed + savings batching, replayed through the same simulate(); reported as a separate KPI row
Two pickers with aisle congestion: time-stepped replay where a picker waits when the next aisle cell is occupied; wait seconds reported
Second held-out month (Oct 2011) scored with the Nov-tuned layout to show transfer
Layout geometry sliders (aisles 6–12, bays 5–10, middle cross-aisle) with full re-score
data_plan: Dataset: Online Retail II, UCI ML Repository id 502, CC BY 4.0; cite Chen, D. (2019), Online Retail II, UCI Machine Learning Repository, https://doi.org/10.24432/C5CG6D. Obtain the verified mirror (UCI zip truncates from campus): `curl -L -o data/raw/online_retail_II.parquet "https://huggingface.co/datasets/vancevo/online-retail-ii/resolve/main/data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet"` (7.16 MB, 1,067,371 rows; columns Invoice, StockCode, Description, Quantity, InvoiceDate, Price, Customer_ID, Country). Fallback: Kaggle anonymous `https://www.kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/download/mashlyn/online-retail-ii-uci` (CSV). Raw file git-ignored; `data/README.md` has the download command and checksum. Month: November 2011 (peak season; both years' sheets are in the parquet so filter by InvoiceDate). Preprocessing (`python -I prep/prep.py --parquet data/raw/online_retail_II.parquet --month 2011-11 --top 100 --out web/public/data/orders_2011-11.json`): drop C-invoices, Quantity ≤ 0, Price ≤ 0, non-product StockCodes (regex ^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$), exact duplicate rows (count logged); one pick line per (Invoice, StockCode); top-100 SKUs by pick lines; orders = invoices with ≥1 covered line, with timestamps; coverage % recorded; co-pick pair counts for the top-100. Output ≈ 400–700 KB gzipped (int indices). Held-out: chronological split inside the month: tune = invoices dated 1–15 Nov, held-out = 16–30 Nov; the optimizer and the player's optimisation session use tune only; every KPI is reported on both; optional second held-out month Oct 2011 via `--month 2011-10`. Warehouse geometry is team-designed and stated in README and in-app: 8 aisles, racks both sides, 7 bays per side at 1.5 m pitch, 3.0 m aisle pitch, 2.5 m cross-aisles, dock front-left, 112 slots (100 SKUs + 12 empty), walking speed 1.2 m/s, 8 s per pick line, single level; original layout = StockCode-sorted assignment (arbitrary, declared; seeded-random alternative in a dropdown). Attribution: README "Dataset attribution and licence" section plus an in-app Data panel with the citation and all cleaning counts.
architecture: Components: (1) `prep/prep.py` (offline, Python 3.12) → `web/public/data/orders_2011-11.json`. (2) `web/src/sim/` pure TS, no DOM: `layout.ts` (graph builder, Dijkstra all-pairs, path extraction), `route.ts` (heldKarp, nn2opt, sShape, returnPolicy), `simulate.ts` (score(assignment, orders, params, policy) → totals + per-order + optional paths), `slotting.ts` (abcBaseline, annealer with delta eval + memo + inverted index, mulberry32), `explain.ts` (slot card, move breakdown). (3) `web/src/worker.ts` wraps sim with the message protocol (INIT/SCORE/DELTA/ABC/PATH/EXPLAIN_SLOT/ANNEAL_*); one worker instance, transferable Float32Arrays. (4) `web/src/store.ts` zustand 5: data, layoutCfg, assignment (Int16Array slot→sku), params, policy, scores {original, abc, sa, player} × {tune, test}, anneal state, selection, scrubDay. (5) `web/src/scene/` R3F: Floor+Racks (InstancedMesh), Boxes (instanced + labels + hover/select/drag), Picker + GhostPicker, PathLine, HeatLayer (instanceColor writer), CameraRig (presets), Effects (Bloom/SMAA with quality toggle). (6) `web/src/ui/`: TopBar (data badge, KPI strip), SlidersPanel, OrderList (virtualised, hover → PATH), OptimizerPanel (energy curve, temperature, feed, play/pause/step/inject/finish), SlotInspector (cause card + affinity lines), EvidencePanel (table mirrors eval/results.md), Leaderboard, Limitations. (7) `eval/run.ts` (tsx, Node) imports `src/sim` and writes `eval/results.md` with commit hash; `eval/layouts/*.json` for SA seeds and player layouts; `public/data/layouts/sa_seed42.json` pre-run for instant load. Data flow: JSON fetch → store → worker INIT → UI dispatches SCORE/DELTA/ANNEAL → results into store → scene reads assignment + paths + heat; animation only consumes worker paths. Compute: 100% in the browser (main thread renders, worker simulates); no backend, no keys, no env secrets (`.env.example` contains only VITE_APP_URL for QR). Deployment: Vite static build on Vercel Hobby (vercel.json: immutable cache headers for /assets and /data; SPA rewrite); mirror on Cloudflare Pages as fallback; `npm run preview` locally as third fallback. Repo layout: README.md, DEV_LOG.md, LICENSE (MIT), .env.example, docs/architecture.md (Mermaid), docs/pitch/*.pptx, docs/demo/script.md, data/README.md, prep/, web/, eval/.
stack: Node 22 LTS, npm; vite 8.3.5; @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1.2; typescript 5.x; vitest (latest 3.x) for sim unit tests; tsx for eval/run.ts

build_plan:
Now 21:30 IST; feature freeze 11:00 IST 22 Oct; submit 14:45. Four Claude agents on branches (feat/sim, feat/scene, feat/ui, chore/infra), fast-forward merges to main at least hourly (Agent D owns the cadence), humans review/own modules as they land.

Agent A — Data + simulation core (~9.5 h): 21:45–22:45 prep.py + data/README (counts, coverage) → commit `data: Nov 2011 top-100 JSON`; 22:45–23:45 layout.ts graph + Dijkstra + path extraction + vitest; 23:45–01:45 route.ts (Held–Karp ≤10, NN+2-opt/Or-opt, S-shape, Return) + tests (DP vs brute force n≤7); 01:45–02:15 simulate.ts + abcBaseline; 02:15–04:45 slotting.ts annealer with inverted index, memo, delta breakdown, T0 calibration, seeded PRNG + delta-equals-full-recompute test; 04:45–05:45 worker.ts protocol incl. watch/fast/pause/inject/finish; 05:45–06:45 eval/run.ts → eval/results.md (5 SA seeds, policy ablation, runtimes) + pre-run sa_seed42.json; 06:45–07:15 explain.ts (slot card, lookahead).

Agent B — 3D scene (~11 h): 21:45–22:45 Vite+R3F scaffold, floor/racks InstancedMesh from layoutCfg, dock, lights, camera presets → deployed "walking skeleton" with Agent D by 23:00; 22:45–00:15 boxes (instanced, labels, colour by rank), hover/select states; 00:15–02:15 picker + ghost, path following with speed/replaySpeed, growing Line, counters wired to store; 02:15–04:15 click-to-swap + DragControls with snap + box move tweens (queue used by ABC and annealer); 04:15–05:45 ghost race mode (two pickers on the same order list, divergent counters), heat layer via instanceColor; 05:45–06:45 Effects (Bloom/SMAA, quality toggle, dpr cap, demand frameloop), top-down ortho toggle; 06:45–08:15 affinity lines for the slot inspector, ABC matching animation hooks, perf pass on a weak laptop (target <150 draw calls, >45 fps High, >60 fps Low).

Agent C — Explorable UI (~10.5 h): 21:45–22:45 app shell, store, data loading, Data badge; 22:45–00:15 KPI strip + Before/ABC/After/Player × tune/held-out table with motion counters; 00:15–01:45 sliders panel (speed, pick s, policy, min-lines, order set, geometry, middle cross-aisle, replay speed) wired to worker SCORE with debounce; 01:45–02:45 order list (virtualised, hover → PATH, click → animate), hero order from demo.json; 02:45–05:15 optimizer panel (energy curve + temperature SVG, move feed, play/pause/step/inject/finish, seed display); 05:15–06:45 slot inspector cause card + explain-a-move toasts + hover lookahead; 06:45–07:45 month scrubber with prefix sums, Evidence panel mirroring eval/results.md, Limitations card; 07:45–08:15 leaderboard (localStorage, export/import JSON).

Agent D — Integration, QA, docs, process (~8 h, spread): 21:35 public repo init (README skeleton with all 7 required sections, .env.example, DEV_LOG.md noting 18:00–21:30 planning, LICENSE MIT, .gitignore) → first commit by 21:45; 23:00 Vercel + Cloudflare deploy of the skeleton, URLs in README; hourly merge/commit cron (45-min reminder), conventional messages, tags mvp-m1/m2/m3, eval-frozen, feature-freeze; 02:00 and 06:00 integration smoke tests on a second laptop + phone; 07:00–09:00 README (Mermaid architecture, data rules, geometry table, eval table paste from results.md, limitations, AI-tools declaration, team/module ownership), DEV_LOG (decisions, experiments table, rejected: OR-Tools/backends/WebGPU/Theatre.js); python-pptx deck skeleton (10 slides) with placeholders for screenshots.

Integration/QA checkpoints (all agents + humans): 01:30 M1–M3 demonstrable end-to-end (tag mvp-m3); 03:30 annealer live in 3D; 05:30 ghost race + inspector + heat; 07:30 eval + README; 09:30 polish, stretch (batching/two pickers only if green); 11:00 freeze. Humans: 11:00–12:30 re-run `npm run eval`, verify app numbers = README numbers, finalize DEV_LOG; 12:30–13:30 record ≤5-min demo + 3-min YouTube cut, finish .pptx with 1920×1080 screenshots; 13:30–14:15 LinkedIn + X posts (#NEXAI2026, URLs, clip); 14:15–14:45 smoke test the deployed URL on a different laptop and phone; 14:45 submit. Q&A cards (10 × 20 s) drafted by 13:00; each human owns named modules (sim / scene / ui / data+eval).
risks: Average-laptop performance (projector laptop, integrated GPU): mitigate with InstancedMesh for racks/boxes/floor tiles (<150 draw calls), dpr cap 1.5, frameloop='demand' when idle, Bloom/SSAO behind a quality toggle with auto-drop below 40 fps, top-down 2D ortho mode as a last resort; test on a weak laptop at 02:00 and 06:00.

Annealer too slow to feel live: inverted SKU→orders index + per-order cost cache + stop-set memo + DP cap 8 in the inner loop; 'watch' mode is throttled by design and 'Finish fast' completes in seconds; a pre-run sa_seed42.json layout ships so the demo never depends on a live run finishing.
Held–Karp blow-up on large orders: hard cap n ≤ 10 (stops dedupe by aisle cell first), NN + 2-opt/Or-opt above; min-lines slider and order-size histogram make the distribution visible.

3D drag-and-drop is fiddly on stage: click-to-select/click-to-swap is the primary interaction and is what the script uses; DragControls is an enhancement; Escape cancels; every move is a tweened queue so nothing teleports.

Judges doubt the twin is data-driven: invoice IDs on screen during replay, Data badge with cleaning counts and coverage %, click any slot to see StockCode/description/picks from the JSON, Replay twice gives identical numbers (seed displayed).

Top-100 coverage is a minority of order lines: say it on screen and in README ('forward-pick area for the top-100 SKUs; orders filtered to covered lines; coverage = X%'); prep.py takes --top for future scaling.
Held-out gain is small or negative for SA: report it anyway with in-sample beside it; the ABC baseline and policy ablation still carry the evaluation story; 5-seed mean±sd shown.

Hourly-commit rule and bulk-dump suspicion: Agent D owns a 45-min reminder, agents commit on feature branches continuously, main receives meaningful merges hourly, eval test set (split) committed before any tuning commit, DEV_LOG timestamps.
Venue Wi-Fi: static site is ~1.5 MB gz and fully cached after first load; Cloudflare mirror; `npm run preview` on the demo laptop; phone hotspot; backup MP4.
Scope creep from stretch goals: strict order after M1–M3: heat → leaderboard → co-op optimizer polish → batching → two pickers; anything not green at 09:30 is cut and listed under 'What's next'.
honesty_plan: Every number on screen is produced by the same `simulate()` that `npm run eval` runs headlessly; the Evidence panel shows the eval table with the commit hash and timestamp and the README pastes that file verbatim, so README = app = deck by construction. Held-out: chronological split (1–15 Nov tune / 16–30 Nov held-out) committed in the data JSON before any optimizer commit; SA and the player's optimisation session see only tune; all KPIs are reported on both sets with the held-out column highlighted; SA reported as mean±sd over 5 seeds (seed 42 shipped) and the in-sample vs held-out gap is called out as evidence of over-fitting, not hidden. Baselines: Original layout explicitly declared as StockCode-sorted (arbitrary), ABC/COI baseline as the must-have target, routing-policy ablation so 'optimal routing' is not conflated with 'better slotting'. Data rules in README and in-app: C-invoices removed, Quantity ≤ 0 and Price ≤ 0 removed, non-product StockCode regex listed with the removed codes, exact duplicates removed, one pick line per (Invoice, StockCode), top-100 by pick lines, coverage % stated, GBP irrelevant to distance but noted; dataset attributed with UCI id 502, DOI and CC BY 4.0; the HF parquet mirror is named as the download path with the UCI file as the canonical source. Modelling assumptions written in README and shown in a Limitations card: single-level racks, team-designed geometry (table of every dimension), constant 1.2 m/s and 8 s per line (both sliders), no congestion/batching/replenishment/cart capacity in MVP, no real layout exists for this retailer, one month only, the twin models a forward-pick area for 100 SKUs.
